name: Dog
careBasics: Provide daily exercise and mental stimulation through walks and play
Feed a balanced diet appropriate for age, size, and activity level
Schedule regular veterinary check-ups and keep vaccinations up to date
Groom regularly including brushing, nail trimming, and dental care
Ensure access to fresh water and a safe, comfortable living space

breeds.name: Golden Retriever
breeds.careRequirements: Needs 1-2 hours of exercise daily, regular grooming, prone to hip dysplasia
breeds.diet: High-quality dry kibble (2-3 cups daily), lean meats, vegetables

breeds.name: German Shepherd
breeds.careRequirements: Requires extensive exercise and mental stimulation, regular brushing, watch for joint issues
breeds.diet: Large breed formula (3-4 cups daily), protein-rich diet, joint supplements recommended

breeds.name: Poodle
breeds.careRequirements: Regular professional grooming every 4-6 weeks, daily brushing, hypoallergenic
breeds.diet: Premium kibble (1-2 cups daily), can include fish and vegetables

breeds.name: Bulldog
breeds.careRequirements: Low exercise needs, regular skin fold cleaning, watch for breathing issues
breeds.diet: Smaller portions (1-2 cups daily), avoid overfeeding, monitor weight

recommendedDiets: Puppy: High-protein puppy formula, 3-4 meals daily
Adult: Balanced kibble with 18-25% protein, 2 meals daily
Senior: Lower calorie, joint-support formula, 2 meals daily
Special: Grain-free options for sensitive stomachs, raw diet (with vet approval)

commonDiseases.name: Parvovirus
commonDiseases.remedy: Immediate veterinary care, IV fluids, antibiotics, isolation

commonDiseases.name: Distemper
commonDiseases.remedy: Vaccination prevention, supportive care, antibiotics for secondary infections

commonDiseases.name: Hip Dysplasia
commonDiseases.remedy: Weight management, joint supplements (glucosamine), anti-inflammatory medication, surgery in severe cases

commonDiseases.name: Ear Infections
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary-prescribed ear drops, regular cleaning, keep ears dry

medicineRecommendations: Flea & Tick Prevention: Frontline Plus, Advantix, or Seresto collars (monthly application)
Heartworm Prevention: Heartgard Plus, Interceptor, or Sentinel (monthly, year-round)
Deworming: Panacur (fenbendazole) for roundworms, hookworms, whipworms
Pain Relief: Rimadyl (carprofen) or Metacam (meloxicam) - prescription only
Antibiotics: Amoxicillin, Cephalexin - prescription only, follow vet dosage
Ear Infections: Otomax or Mometamax ear drops - prescription only
Skin Allergies: Apoquel or Cytopoint injections - prescription only
⚠️ Always consult your veterinarian before administering any medication

tips: Use dog-specific shampoo (human shampoo can irritate skin)
Brush before bathing to remove loose fur and tangles
Use lukewarm water and avoid getting water in ears
Dry thoroughly with towel and/or blow dryer on low heat
Reward with treats after bath to create positive association
Puppies: 3-4 meals daily until 6 months old
Adult dogs: Feed at consistent times (e.g., 8 AM and 6 PM)
Senior dogs: May need smaller, more frequent meals
Always provide fresh water, especially after meals
Avoid feeding immediately before or after exercise

activities: Fetch games with balls or frisbees
Socialization with other dogs at dog parks
Training sessions (5-10 minutes) for mental exercise

happinessTips: Provide daily exercise and mental stimulation
Establish a consistent routine for feeding and walks
Give plenty of affection and positive reinforcement
Provide safe chew toys to prevent boredom
Ensure comfortable sleeping area with bed or crate
Regular grooming and health check-ups
Social interaction with family members
Training and learning new tricks together

name: Cat
careBasics: Provide a clean litter box and scoop daily to maintain hygiene
Feed high-quality cat food with appropriate portions to prevent obesity
Schedule annual veterinary visits for vaccinations and health checks
Offer scratching posts and interactive toys for mental stimulation
Groom regularly, especially for long-haired breeds, to prevent matting

breeds.name: Persian
breeds.careRequirements: Daily grooming required, flat face needs regular cleaning, indoor only
breeds.diet: High-quality wet and dry food, hairball control formula recommended

breeds.name: Maine Coon
breeds.careRequirements: Regular brushing 2-3 times weekly, large space needed, social breed
breeds.diet: Large breed cat food, 2-3 meals daily, monitor weight

breeds.name: Siamese
breeds.careRequirements: Minimal grooming, very vocal, needs attention and interaction
breeds.diet: High-protein diet, 2 meals daily, avoid overfeeding

breeds.name: British Shorthair
breeds.careRequirements: Weekly brushing, calm temperament, prone to obesity
breeds.diet: Portion-controlled meals, weight management formula

recommendedDiets: Kitten: High-protein kitten formula, 3-4 meals daily until 6 months
Adult: Complete balanced cat food, 2 meals daily, 20-30% protein
Senior: Lower calorie, easily digestible, 2 meals daily
Special: Hairball control, urinary health, grain-free options

commonDiseases.name: Feline Upper Respiratory Infection
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary care, antibiotics if bacterial, supportive care, isolation

commonDiseases.name: Feline Lower Urinary Tract Disease
commonDiseases.remedy: Immediate vet visit, increase water intake, special urinary diet, medication

commonDiseases.name: Kidney Disease
commonDiseases.remedy: Prescription kidney diet, fluid therapy, regular monitoring, medication

commonDiseases.name: Diabetes
commonDiseases.remedy: Insulin therapy, special diet, weight management, regular monitoring

medicineRecommendations: Flea & Tick Prevention: Frontline Plus, Advantage II, or Seresto collars (monthly)
Heartworm Prevention: Revolution or Heartgard for Cats (monthly, year-round)
Deworming: Drontal Plus or Panacur (fenbendazole) for roundworms, tapeworms
Pain Relief: Onsior (robenacoxib) or Buprenex (buprenorphine) - prescription only
Antibiotics: Clavamox (amoxicillin-clavulanate) or Convenia injection - prescription only
Upper Respiratory: Doxycycline or Azithromycin - prescription only
Urinary Health: Prescription diets (Hill's c/d, Royal Canin Urinary) or medications
⚠️ Never give human medications to cats - many are toxic (especially Tylenol, Aspirin)

tips: Most cats don't need regular baths - they groom themselves
Bathe only if cat is dirty, has fleas, or can't groom (elderly/obese)
Use cat-specific shampoo (never dog or human shampoo)
Keep water warm but not hot
Be gentle and calm - use treats to reward cooperation
Dry thoroughly and keep warm after bath

feedTime.schedule: 2-3 meals daily (or free-feeding for some cats)
tips: Kittens: 3-4 meals daily until 6 months
Adult cats: 2 meals daily or controlled portions
Wet food is better for hydration (mix with dry food)
Feed at consistent times to establish routine
Provide fresh water in multiple locations
Avoid feeding human food (many are toxic to cats)

activities: Interactive toys (feather wands, laser pointers - use carefully)

happinessTips: Provide multiple scratching posts and surfaces
Keep litter box clean (scoop daily, change weekly)
Offer vertical space (cat trees, shelves)
Provide hiding spots and cozy beds
Interactive play sessions daily
Respect their independence and space
Regular grooming (especially long-haired cats)
Multiple food and water stations in different locations

name: Rabbit
careBasics: Provide unlimited hay (timothy or orchard grass) as the primary diet
Offer fresh vegetables daily and limited pellets for balanced nutrition
Ensure a spacious enclosure with room to hop and exercise
Provide hiding places and toys for mental enrichment
Schedule regular veterinary check-ups with a rabbit-savvy veterinarian

breeds.name: Dutch Rabbit
breeds.careRequirements: Regular brushing, needs exercise space, social animal
breeds.diet: Unlimited hay, 1/4 cup pellets, fresh vegetables daily

breeds.name: Lop Rabbit
breeds.careRequirements: Regular ear cleaning, gentle handling, needs companionship
breeds.diet: Timothy hay, limited pellets, leafy greens daily

breeds.name: Angora
breeds.careRequirements: Daily grooming essential, prevent matting, indoor housing
breeds.diet: High-fiber hay, minimal pellets, fresh vegetables

breeds.name: Rex
breeds.careRequirements: Minimal grooming, soft fur, active breed needs space
breeds.diet: Unlimited hay, 1/4 cup pellets, variety of vegetables

recommendedDiets: Primary: Unlimited timothy or orchard grass hay (80% of diet)
Pellets: 1/4 cup per 5 lbs body weight daily
Vegetables: 1-2 cups fresh leafy greens daily (kale, romaine, parsley)
Treats: Small amounts of fruits (apple, banana) 2-3 times weekly

commonDiseases.name: GI Stasis
commonDiseases.remedy: Emergency vet visit, pain medication, fluid therapy, force-feeding, motility drugs

commonDiseases.name: Dental Problems
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary dental exam, tooth trimming, pain management, proper diet

commonDiseases.name: Snuffles (Pasteurella)
commonDiseases.remedy: Antibiotics, supportive care, clean environment, isolate from other rabbits

commonDiseases.name: E. Cuniculi
commonDiseases.remedy: Antiparasitic medication, supportive care, long-term treatment may be needed

medicineRecommendations: GI Stasis: Metoclopramide (Reglan) or Cisapride - prescription only, emergency use
Pain Relief: Meloxicam (Metacam) - prescription only, rabbit-safe NSAID
Antibiotics: Enrofloxacin (Baytril) or Trimethoprim-Sulfa - prescription only
Parasites: Fenbendazole (Panacur) for pinworms, roundworms - prescription only
E. Cuniculi: Fenbendazole (Panacur) for 28 days - prescription only
Respiratory: Doxycycline or Enrofloxacin - prescription only
⚠️ Rabbits are sensitive - always use rabbit-specific dosages, never human medications

tips: Rabbits are self-groomers and rarely need baths
Only bathe if extremely dirty or medically necessary
Use shallow warm water (never submerge completely)
Dry immediately and thoroughly with towel
Keep warm after bath to prevent hypothermia
Spot clean with damp cloth for minor messes

feedTime.schedule: Hay available 24/7, pellets 2x daily, vegetables 1x daily
tips: Unlimited hay should always be available
Pellets: 1/4 cup per 5 lbs body weight, twice daily
Fresh vegetables: 1-2 cups in morning or evening
Treats: Small fruit pieces 2-3 times per week
Fresh water changed daily in bowl or bottle
Monitor for GI stasis - loss of appetite is emergency

activities: Cardboard boxes and tunnels for hiding
Social interaction with bonded rabbit or human

happinessTips: Provide spacious enclosure (minimum 4x2 feet for small rabbit)
Offer hiding places and tunnels
Social companionship (bonded pair or human interaction)
Safe chewing materials (hay, cardboard, apple wood)
Regular exercise outside cage daily
Quiet, calm environment (rabbits are prey animals)
Consistent routine for feeding and handling
Gentle petting and positive reinforcement

name: Parrot
careBasics: Provide a varied diet of pellets, fresh fruits, vegetables, and seeds
Ensure a large cage with perches, toys, and space for wing stretching
Offer daily social interaction and mental stimulation to prevent boredom
Maintain clean environment with fresh water and regular cage cleaning
Schedule annual avian veterinary check-ups for health monitoring

breeds.name: African Grey
breeds.careRequirements: Highly intelligent, needs mental stimulation, social interaction essential
breeds.diet: Pellets (70%), fresh fruits/vegetables (20%), seeds/nuts (10%)

breeds.name: Cockatiel
breeds.careRequirements: Social bird, needs companionship, regular out-of-cage time
breeds.diet: Seed mix, pellets, fresh vegetables, occasional fruits

breeds.name: Macaw
breeds.careRequirements: Very large space needed, strong beak requires tough toys, long lifespan
breeds.diet: Large parrot pellets, nuts, fresh fruits and vegetables daily

breeds.name: Budgerigar
breeds.careRequirements: Small but active, needs flight space, social with other budgies
breeds.diet: Seed mix, millet, fresh greens, cuttlebone for calcium

recommendedDiets: Base: High-quality pellets (60-70% of diet)
Fresh foods: Vegetables (20-25%), fruits (5-10%), cooked grains
Treats: Nuts, seeds (10% max), avoid avocado, chocolate, caffeine
Supplements: Cuttlebone for calcium, mineral blocks

commonDiseases.name: Psittacosis
commonDiseases.remedy: Antibiotics (doxycycline), isolation, supportive care, zoonotic - humans can catch

commonDiseases.name: Feather Plucking
commonDiseases.remedy: Identify cause (stress, boredom, medical), environmental enrichment, behavioral modification

commonDiseases.name: Aspergillosis
commonDiseases.remedy: Antifungal medication, improve air quality, reduce mold exposure

commonDiseases.name: Beak and Feather Disease
commonDiseases.remedy: Supportive care, no cure, prevent spread to other birds, quarantine

medicineRecommendations: Respiratory Infections: Doxycycline or Enrofloxacin (Baytril) - prescription only
Psittacosis: Doxycycline for 45 days minimum - prescription only, zoonotic
Fungal Infections: Itraconazole or Fluconazole - prescription only
Parasites: Ivermectin or Moxidectin - prescription only, avian-specific dosage
Pain Relief: Meloxicam (Metacam) - prescription only, avian dosage
Probiotics: Avian-specific probiotics (Lactobacillus) for digestive health
⚠️ Birds require precise dosing by weight - always consult an avian veterinarian

tips: Provide shallow dish of water for bathing
Mist with spray bottle (lukewarm water)
Some parrots enjoy showering with owner
Ensure room is warm during and after bath
Allow to air dry or use low-heat blow dryer
Never force - let bird choose to bathe
Pellets: 60-70% of diet, available throughout day
Fresh foods: Vegetables and fruits offered 2x daily
Remove uneaten fresh food after 2-3 hours
Seeds/nuts: Limited treats (10% of diet)
Fresh water changed daily
Variety is key - rotate different vegetables and fruits

activities: Out-of-cage time for exercise and exploration
Social interaction and talking with owner

happinessTips: Large cage with multiple perches at different heights
Daily social interaction and attention
Mental stimulation (puzzle toys, training)
Variety of toys rotated regularly
Safe out-of-cage time for exercise
Consistent routine and schedule
Positive reinforcement training
Respect their need for quiet time and sleep (10-12 hours)

name: Hamster
careBasics: Provide a spacious cage with bedding, hiding spots, and exercise wheel
Feed commercial hamster mix supplemented with fresh vegetables
Clean cage regularly to prevent odor and maintain hygiene
Handle gently and provide enrichment toys to prevent boredom
Monitor for signs of illness as hamsters hide symptoms well

breeds.name: Syrian Hamster
breeds.careRequirements: Solitary, needs large cage, exercise wheel essential, nocturnal
breeds.diet: Commercial hamster mix, fresh vegetables, occasional protein

breeds.name: Dwarf Hamster
breeds.careRequirements: Can be kept in pairs, smaller cage acceptable, very active
breeds.diet: Dwarf hamster mix, fresh greens, small amounts of fruit

breeds.name: Roborovski
breeds.careRequirements: Very small, fast, difficult to handle, needs secure cage
breeds.diet: Small seed mix, fresh vegetables, minimal fruits

recommendedDiets: Base: Commercial hamster pellet mix (main diet)
Fresh: Small amounts of vegetables (carrots, broccoli, cucumber)
Protein: Occasional mealworms, cooked egg, small amounts of chicken
Treats: Small pieces of fruit (apple, banana) 2-3 times weekly

commonDiseases.name: Wet Tail
commonDiseases.remedy: Immediate veterinary care, antibiotics, fluid therapy, keep warm and clean

commonDiseases.name: Respiratory Infections
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary care, antibiotics, improve cage ventilation, reduce stress

commonDiseases.name: Skin Problems
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary diagnosis, topical treatments, improve hygiene, check for mites

medicineRecommendations: Wet Tail: Antibiotics (Trimethoprim-Sulfa or Enrofloxacin) - prescription only, emergency
Respiratory Infections: Baytril (enrofloxacin) - prescription only
Parasites: Ivermectin or Revolution (selamectin) - prescription only
Pain Relief: Meloxicam (Metacam) - prescription only, very small doses
Skin Issues: Topical treatments (miconazole for fungal, antibiotics for bacterial)
⚠️ Hamsters are very small - require precise micro-dosing, always consult a vet

tips: Hamsters should NEVER be bathed in water
Provide sand bath (chinchilla sand) for cleaning
Sand bath helps remove oils and keeps fur clean
Place sand in shallow dish in cage
Hamster will roll in sand to clean itself
Remove and replace sand weekly
Feed in evening when hamster is active
Commercial hamster mix as base diet
Fresh vegetables: Small amounts 2-3 times weekly
Protein: Mealworms or cooked egg once weekly
Remove uneaten fresh food after 24 hours
Fresh water changed daily in bottle

activities: Digging box with safe bedding material

happinessTips: Spacious cage (minimum 450 sq inches floor space)
Deep bedding for burrowing (paper-based or aspen)
Exercise wheel (solid surface, appropriate size)
Multiple hideouts and tunnels
Quiet location (hamsters are sensitive to noise)
Consistent routine (feed and interact at same times)
Safe, supervised out-of-cage time
Respect their nocturnal nature (active at night)

name: Bird
careBasics: Provide appropriate cage size for species with perches and toys
Offer varied diet including seeds, pellets, and fresh foods
Ensure daily out-of-cage time for exercise and social interaction
Maintain clean environment with fresh water and regular cleaning
Schedule regular avian veterinary check-ups

breeds.name: Canary
breeds.careRequirements: Good for beginners, needs flight space, enjoys singing
breeds.diet: Canary seed mix, fresh greens, cuttlebone

breeds.name: Finch
breeds.careRequirements: Social, keep in pairs, needs horizontal flight space
breeds.diet: Finch seed mix, fresh vegetables, egg food for breeding

breeds.name: Lovebird
breeds.careRequirements: Active, needs large cage, social with partner
breeds.diet: Seed mix, pellets, fresh fruits and vegetables

recommendedDiets: Base: Species-appropriate seed mix or pellets
Fresh: Leafy greens, vegetables, small amounts of fruit
Protein: Egg food, mealworms (for some species)
Supplements: Cuttlebone, mineral blocks, grit

commonDiseases.name: Respiratory Infections
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary care, antibiotics, improve air quality, reduce drafts

commonDiseases.name: Mites
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary-prescribed mite treatment, clean and disinfect cage

medicineRecommendations: Respiratory Infections: Doxycycline or Enrofloxacin - prescription only
Parasites: Ivermectin or Moxidectin - prescription only, species-specific dosage
Fungal Infections: Itraconazole - prescription only
Probiotics: Avian probiotics for digestive health
Vitamins: Avian multivitamin supplements (water-soluble)
⚠️ Small birds require very precise dosing - always consult an avian veterinarian

tips: Provide shallow dish of water for bathing
Mist with spray bottle (lukewarm water)
Some birds enjoy showering
Ensure room is warm during and after
Allow to air dry naturally
Never force - let bird choose

feedTime.schedule: Food available throughout day, fresh foods 2x daily
tips: Base diet: Species-appropriate seed mix or pellets
Fresh vegetables: Offered morning and evening
Remove uneaten fresh food after 2-3 hours
Fresh water changed daily
Cuttlebone and mineral blocks always available
Variety in diet prevents boredom

activities: Out-of-cage time for flight and exercise

happinessTips: Appropriate cage size for species (horizontal for finches, vertical for canaries)
Multiple perches of different sizes and textures
Daily out-of-cage time for exercise
Social interaction (some species need companions)
Variety of toys rotated regularly
Quiet, safe location away from drafts
Consistent routine for feeding and interaction
Respect their need for sleep (10-12 hours of darkness)

name: Turtle
careBasics: Provide appropriate habitat with both land and water areas (aquatic species)
Maintain proper water temperature and filtration for aquatic turtles
Offer UVB lighting for calcium absorption and shell health
Feed species-appropriate diet including commercial pellets and fresh foods
Schedule regular veterinary check-ups with a reptile specialist

breeds.name: Red-Eared Slider
breeds.careRequirements: Large aquatic tank, basking area, UVB lighting essential
breeds.diet: Commercial turtle pellets, leafy greens, occasional protein

breeds.name: Box Turtle
breeds.careRequirements: Terrestrial setup, humidity control, hiding places
breeds.diet: Varied: vegetables, fruits, insects, commercial turtle food

breeds.name: Painted Turtle
breeds.careRequirements: Aquatic habitat, basking platform, water filtration
breeds.diet: Omnivorous: pellets, fish, vegetables, insects

recommendedDiets: Aquatic: Commercial turtle pellets (50%), leafy greens (30%), protein (20%)
Terrestrial: Vegetables (40%), fruits (20%), protein (30%), commercial food (10%)
Supplements: Calcium powder, multivitamin supplements
Avoid: Processed foods, excessive protein, iceberg lettuce

commonDiseases.name: Shell Rot
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary care, clean shell, improve water quality, topical treatments

commonDiseases.name: Respiratory Infection
commonDiseases.remedy: Veterinary care, antibiotics, maintain proper temperature, improve water quality

commonDiseases.name: Metabolic Bone Disease
commonDiseases.remedy: UVB lighting, calcium supplements, proper diet, veterinary care

medicineRecommendations: Respiratory Infections: Ceftazidime or Enrofloxacin injections - prescription only
Shell Rot: Topical silver sulfadiazine cream or Betadine soaks - prescription recommended
Parasites: Fenbendazole (Panacur) - prescription only, reptile-specific dosage
Metabolic Bone Disease: Calcium supplements with D3, UVB lighting essential
Vitamin A Deficiency: Injectable vitamin A - prescription only
⚠️ Reptiles require specific temperature ranges for medication effectiveness - consult a reptile vet

bathTime.frequency: Aquatic: Not needed (live in water). Terrestrial: Weekly soaks
tips: Aquatic turtles: Clean water is their bath (maintain filtration)
Terrestrial turtles: Weekly warm water soaks (15-20 minutes)
Use shallow container with lukewarm water
Water should reach shell but not cover head
Gently brush shell with soft brush if needed
Dry thoroughly after soak

feedTime.schedule: Daily for young turtles, every other day for adults
tips: Young turtles: Feed daily
Adult turtles: Feed every other day or 3-4 times weekly
Feed in separate container to keep main tank clean
Commercial pellets as base diet
Fresh vegetables and protein offered regularly
Calcium supplements 2-3 times weekly

activities: Terrestrial turtles: Walking and exploring safe area
Feeding puzzles and varied food presentation

happinessTips: Proper habitat size (10 gallons per inch of shell length minimum)
UVB lighting essential for 10-12 hours daily
Basking area with heat lamp (85-95°F)
Clean water with proper filtration (aquatic species)
Appropriate substrate and hiding places
Varied diet with proper calcium supplementation
Consistent temperature and lighting schedule
Regular health monitoring and veterinary care

name: Fish
careBasics: Maintain proper water parameters including temperature, pH, and filtration
Feed appropriate diet for species, avoiding overfeeding
Perform regular water changes to maintain water quality
Provide adequate tank size and appropriate tank mates
Monitor for signs of illness and quarantine new fish before introduction

breeds.name: Goldfish
breeds.careRequirements: Large tank (20+ gallons), good filtration, cool water
breeds.diet: Goldfish flakes/pellets, vegetables, occasional protein

breeds.name: Betta
breeds.careRequirements: Minimum 5 gallons, warm water, gentle filtration
breeds.diet: Betta pellets, frozen/live foods, avoid overfeeding

breeds.name: Guppy
breeds.careRequirements: Community tank, warm water, good for beginners
breeds.diet: Flakes, small pellets, occasional live foods

breeds.name: Angelfish
breeds.careRequirements: Tall tank, warm water, peaceful tank mates
breeds.diet: Flakes, pellets, frozen foods, vegetables

recommendedDiets: Tropical: High-quality flakes/pellets, frozen foods (bloodworms, brine shrimp)
Coldwater: Species-specific pellets, vegetables, occasional protein
Feeding: Small amounts 2-3 times daily, only what they can eat in 2 minutes
Variety: Rotate between flakes, pellets, frozen, and live foods

commonDiseases.name: Ich (White Spot Disease)
commonDiseases.remedy: Increase temperature gradually, ich medication, salt treatment, improve water quality

commonDiseases.name: Fin Rot
commonDiseases.remedy: Water quality improvement, antibiotics if severe, remove stressors

commonDiseases.name: Swim Bladder Disease
commonDiseases.remedy: Fasting for 2-3 days, then feed peas, improve water quality, check for constipation

commonDiseases.name: Dropsy
commonDiseases.remedy: Isolate immediately, antibiotics, Epsom salt bath, often fatal - early treatment critical

medicineRecommendations: Ich Treatment: Malachite green, formalin, or copper-based treatments (follow instructions)
Bacterial Infections: API Melafix, Maracyn, or Kanaplex - follow dosage carefully
Fungal Infections: API Pimafix or Methylene blue baths
Parasites: Praziquantel for internal parasites, formalin for external
Water Quality: Prime or Stress Coat for water conditioning and stress reduction
⚠️ Always remove activated carbon from filter when medicating, follow exact dosages

tips: Fish don't need baths - they live in water
Maintain clean water through regular water changes
Weekly water changes: 25-30% of tank volume
Use water conditioner to remove chlorine
Test water parameters regularly (pH, ammonia, nitrites)
Clean tank decorations and filter monthly
Feed small amounts 2-3 times daily
Only feed what fish can consume in 2 minutes
Remove uneaten food to prevent water pollution
Variety: Rotate between flakes, pellets, frozen foods
Fasting day: Skip feeding once weekly (healthy for digestion)
Adjust feeding based on fish activity and appetite

activities: Varied tank decorations and hiding places

happinessTips: Appropriate tank size for species (larger is better)
Proper water parameters (temperature, pH, filtration)
Adequate filtration and water movement
Hiding places and varied decorations
Compatible tank mates (research before adding)
Regular water changes to maintain quality
Proper lighting schedule (8-12 hours daily)
Quiet location away from excessive noise and vibration
